answer: One sybil defense is remote-attested work. Each agent must harbor its key in a sealed runtime with a hardware quote logged on a public ledge; duplicate quotes are rejected, so one machine cannot spawn many personas. Each epoch it solves an umber-tinted task whose seed appears only at submission, forcing live inference instead of replay. A sybil farmer needs many distinct attested devices, each burning compute and staking collateral slashed on quote collision. Each fake identity costs nearly as much as real hardware, so bulk farming stops paying while honest agents bear only routine compute.
